top_choice_rationale: Base editing is a defined chemical conversion (cytosine or adenine deamination on DNA) that avoids double-strand cleavage. The two editor classes are separate inventions: the cytosine editor needed uracil glycosylase inhibition and nickase-directed repair bias, and the adenine editor needed directed evolution of TadA. Komor and Gaudelli are therefore needed alongside Liu. Both editors have been reproduced and extended independently and have reached patients, and the open points (Target-AID priority, long-term off-target safety) are less severe than the open points on the alternatives. It is more precisely attributable than targeted protein degradation, where bifunctional degraders and cereblon glues are hard to separate in three names.
